{
  "dataset_name": "spambase",
  "model_family": "tree",
  "schema_generator": "gemini-3.1-pro-preview",
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "features": [
    {
      "name": "capital_run_length_ratio",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Ratio of the longest capital run length to the average capital run length, capturing bursts of capitalization relative to the typical run.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 10000.0],
      "feature_family": "text_statistics",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Tree models can split on this ratio to isolate documents with unusually long, concentrated blocks of capital letters compared to their baseline.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "capital_run_length_longest / np.maximum(capital_run_length_average, 1.0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "total_special_char_freq",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Sum of all character frequency features, representing the overall density of special characters in the text.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 100.0],
      "feature_family": "character_frequencies",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Provides a single aggregate measure of special character usage, allowing trees to easily separate text with high overall symbol density.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "char_freq_0 + char_freq_1 + char_freq_2 + char_freq_3 + char_freq_4 + char_freq_5"
    },
    {
      "name": "high_capital_run_indicator",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Boolean indicator for whether the longest capital run length exceeds 50 characters.",
      "value_range": [0, 1],
      "feature_family": "text_statistics",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Explicitly flags extreme capitalization, saving the tree model from having to find this specific threshold during early splits.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where(capital_run_length_longest > 50, 1, 0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "frequent_words_sum",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Sum of the frequencies of several commonly occurring words (indices 18, 20, 24, 26) to capture a broader thematic presence.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 100.0],
      "feature_family": "word_frequencies",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Aggregates related high-frequency word features, reducing dimensionality and providing a stronger, more stable signal for tree splits.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "word_freq_18 + word_freq_20 + word_freq_24 + word_freq_26"
    },
    {
      "name": "capital_run_length_total_log",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Log-transformed total number of capital letters, compressing the long tail of the distribution.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 15.0],
      "feature_family": "text_statistics",
      "expected_model_benefit": "While trees are invariant to monotonic transformations, log-scaling can help stabilize variance and improve the resolution of splits in the lower range of values.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.log1p(capital_run_length_total)"
    },
    {
      "name": "char_freq_3_exceeds_threshold",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Indicator for whether char_freq_3 is greater than 0.5, capturing a significant presence of this specific character.",
      "value_range": [0, 1],
      "feature_family": "character_frequencies",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Creates a hard categorical split for a feature with a highly skewed distribution, isolating extreme values directly.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where(char_freq_3 > 0.5, 1, 0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "word_freq_18_20_interaction",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Multiplicative interaction between word_freq_18 and word_freq_20, highlighting documents where both words appear frequently together.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 200.0],
      "feature_family": "word_frequencies",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Exposes a non-linear relationship between two high-frequency words that a tree model would otherwise need multiple splits to approximate.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "word_freq_18 * word_freq_20"
    },
    {
      "name": "capital_run_length_longest_log",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Log-transformed longest capital run length.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 15.0],
      "feature_family": "text_statistics",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Compresses extreme outliers in the longest run length, potentially leading to more balanced and robust tree splits.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.log1p(capital_run_length_longest)"
    },
    {
      "name": "char_freq_4_5_sum",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Sum of char_freq_4 and char_freq_5, combining two potentially related character frequency signals.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 25.0],
      "feature_family": "character_frequencies",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Groups similar character features, allowing the model to split on their combined presence rather than relying on individual, weaker signals.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "char_freq_4 + char_freq_5"
    },
    {
      "name": "word_freq_24_26_max",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "The maximum value between word_freq_24 and word_freq_26, capturing the dominant frequency among these two words.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 30.0],
      "feature_family": "word_frequencies",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Provides a single feature representing the strongest signal from a pair of related words, simplifying the decision boundary for the tree.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.maximum(word_freq_24, word_freq_26)"
    },
    {
      "name": "capital_density_proxy",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Ratio of total capital letters to the longest run, indicating whether capitals are spread out or concentrated in a single block.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 15000.0],
      "feature_family": "text_statistics",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Captures the structural distribution of capital letters, offering a novel interaction that trees can use to differentiate text formatting styles.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "capital_run_length_total / np.maximum(capital_run_length_longest, 1.0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "semantic_urgency_score",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "A semantic assessment of the text's urgency or aggressive tone, derived from the combination of high special character frequencies and long sequences of capital letters.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 10.0],
      "feature_family": "semantic_analysis",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Provides a high-level, interpretable score that synthesizes multiple low-level syntactic features into a single, powerful splitting criterion for tree models.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    }
  ]
}
